Read this first, because it is where most Revlon shoppers end up confused: “Revlon hair dryer” is two different product categories. Revlon’s most-searched products are hot air brush stylers — “revlon hair brush dryer” alone runs around 1,300 searches a month, and the brush-styler group totals roughly 9,930 a month. Those are a different product type, and we hold no sales or review data for them.

This page covers Revlon hair dryers — the conventional dryers. We track one in Canada: the RVDR5034F Compact Travel at about C$19, with 3,491 ratings at 4.4★ selling roughly 3,106 units a month at BSR #5 Amazon.ca data.

And Revlon is not a small player. It holds roughly 12% of Canadian hair dryer unit sales, third behind slopehill and Conair Amazon.ca data. It does it almost entirely in the band where our data shows a 30.3% complaint rate Review analysis.

What we liked about the Revlon RVDR5034F

1. It is the cheapest dryer we track at about C$19. Nothing else in our dataset comes close Amazon.ca data.

2. 3,491 ratings at 4.4★ over 7.5 years. That is a long, stable track record rather than a launch spike, and the sample is large enough to be informative Amazon.ca data.

3. BSR #5 with roughly 3,106 units a month. It is one of the highest-volume dryers in Canada, which means parts of the market clearly find it adequate Amazon.ca data.

4. It is genuinely easy to buy in person. Revlon is stocked in Walmart Canada, Shoppers Drug Mart and Canadian Tire. For a cheap dryer, being able to pick it up and hold it matters Amazon.ca data.

5. It is marketed and sized as a compact travel dryer. A folding handle and small body are real advantages for packing, whatever the voltage situation Manufacturer claim.

What we didn’t like about the Revlon RVDR5034F

1. We could not confirm it is dual voltage. This is the biggest caveat on this page, and it matters specifically because it is sold as a travel dryer. A compact 120V dryer is still unusable in Europe. Voltage was the single most-discussed topic in our entire dataset at 785 mentions Review analysis. Check the product page before relying on it abroad.

2. Budget price band, where complaints are three times as common. Under C$50, our data shows a 30.3% complaint rate across 3,259 reviews, against 9.6% over C$120 across 334 Review analysis.

3. Two sellers with Amazon holding the Buy Box — no brand storefront. Unlike Laifen, Dreame, wavytalk, Aina and Dyson, Revlon has no brand-operated listing here. Warranty complaints are the second-largest cluster in our data at 610 mentions and 81% negative, largely driven by reseller listings where nobody owns the claim (Amazon.ca data, review analysis).

4. It is a compact budget dryer, so airflow is the limitation. Airflow was the most-discussed topic in our dataset at 1,585 mentions, and complaints run one way — too weak for the buyer’s hair Review analysis. A compact dryer at about C$19 is not the tool for dense or long hair.

5. We have not tested it. No measured airflow, noise, weight or dry time. Every measured row reads “not yet tested” — see how we test.

Is Revlon a reliable brand?

The honest answer is that it is a very large budget brand, and the band it competes in is the one our data flags.

What Revlon brings:

FactorAssessment
Canadian unit share~12% — third behind slopehill and Conair
Review base3,491 ratings at 4.4★ on the RVDR5034F
Longevity7.5 years on sale for this listing
Priceabout C$19 — the lowest we track
Retail distributionWalmart Canada, Shoppers Drug Mart, Canadian Tire
Motor technologyConventional
Warranty counterpartyAmazon or a second seller — no brand storefront
Price bandUnder C$50 → 30.3% complaint rate

How to read the 30.3% figure. It is not a criticism of Revlon specifically — it describes the band, which every budget brand competes in. But it is a real difference: a dryer over C$120 has roughly one third the complaint rate in our data Review analysis.

What our dataset says about durability generally: the median reported failure was 5.5 months, and only 0.8% failed out of the box. This is a wear-out category, and the price band is the strongest predictor we found. See how long hair dryers actually last.

Who should buy the Revlon RVDR5034F

Buy it if:

  • You want a cheap second dryer for travel, a gym bag, or a spare bathroom
  • The price of about C$19 is the deciding factor and you accept the band’s reliability characteristics
  • Your hair is short to medium and not especially thick
  • You want to buy in person rather than online
  • You have confirmed the voltage range on the listing if you plan to take it abroad

Do not buy it if:

  • Your hair is thick or long — you want airflow, and this is a compact budget design
  • You need confirmed dual voltage — we could not verify it
  • You want a brand-operated listing and one clear warranty counterparty
  • You are replacing a broken dryer and want an upgrade — moving to the band around C$100 roughly thirds the complaint rate

If you want one dryer for home and travel, the Dreame Pocket Pro at about C$160 is dual voltage and rated 4.6★, and the Dyson Supersonic Travel at about C$400 states universal voltage plainly. Our travel hair dryer guide compares both.

Revlon hair dryer FAQ

Is Revlon a good hair dryer brand? For the price, it is competitive. Revlon holds roughly 12% of Canadian hair dryer unit sales, third behind slopehill and Conair, and its RVDR5034F carries 3,491 ratings at 4.4 stars while selling about 3,106 units a month at BSR #5. The caveat is the price band.

Why does searching for a Revlon hair dryer show brush stylers? Because Revlon’s most-searched products are hot air brushes, not hair dryers — ‘revlon hair brush dryer’ alone is around 1,300 searches a month. Those are a different product category and we hold no sales or review data for them, so this page covers Revlon hair dryers only.

Is the Revlon RVDR5034F dual voltage? We could not confirm the voltage range from the listing data we hold, so treat dual voltage as unverified and check the product page before relying on it abroad. It is marketed and sized as a compact travel dryer, but ‘compact’ describes dimensions, not electricity.

How much does a Revlon hair dryer cost in Canada? The RVDR5034F is about C$19 on Amazon.ca, which makes it the cheapest dryer in our dataset apart from nothing — it is the lowest-priced model we track. It sells roughly 3,106 units a month at BSR #5.

Is the Revlon hair dryer good for thick hair? It is a compact budget dryer, so we would not recommend it for dense or long hair. Airflow was the most-discussed topic in our dataset at 1,585 mentions, and complaints run one way — too weak for the buyer’s hair. For thick hair see our thick hair guide.

Who sells Revlon hair dryers in Canada? On Amazon.ca the RVDR5034F has two sellers with Amazon itself holding the Buy Box, so there is no brand-operated storefront. Revlon is also widely stocked in Walmart Canada, Shoppers Drug Mart and Canadian Tire, which makes it one of the easiest dryers to buy in person.

Our verdict on Revlon hair dryers

Revlon is Canada’s third-largest hair dryer brand by units, and it competes entirely on price.

At about C$19 the RVDR5034F is the cheapest dryer we track, with 3,491 ratings at 4.4★, roughly 3,106 units a month at BSR #5, and a 7.5-year track record. As a cheap second dryer for travel or a spare bathroom, that is a defensible purchase.

Two things to hold against it. It sits in the band where our data shows a 30.3% complaint rate against 9.6% over C$120. And we could not confirm it is dual voltage — which matters because it is sold as a travel dryer, and a compact 120V dryer is still unusable in Europe.

And the honest gap: Revlon’s biggest search category in Canada is hot air brush stylers at roughly 9,930 searches a month, more than every hair dryer query we do cover. We have no data on that product type, so we do not write about it. If you want us to, that is a data-collection job rather than a writing one.
